clue.text: Mass movement started by Arnold going to America

parts.note: Benedict Arnold, the American general who turned traitor; his first name comes first, so it 'starts' the word
US is the usual abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A political mass movement launched by someone called Arnold spreads across the Atlantic to the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass movement' is not a crowd but a section of the Latin Mass; Arnold is the forename-reversed traitor, Benedict Arnold.
explanation.definitionFit: The Benedictus is a sung section of the Mass setting, following the Sanctus, so it is one movement of a choral Mass.

clue.text: Composer comes per motorway, possibly

parts.note: per means by, as in 'by the hour'
a motorway is one kind of road, abbreviated RD

explanation.surface: A composer arrives by way of the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' marks the motorway as only an example of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: William Byrd was the great Elizabethan composer of Masses and madrigals.

clue.text: Wouk showed us its way

parts.note: the American novelist Herman Wouk wrote a 1957 Broadway comedy whose title names the path of the physical world

explanation.surface: The novelist Herman Wouk pointed out how something works.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue turns a play title into a sentence: Wouk 'showed' (staged) the way of the world around us.
explanation.definitionFit: Wouk's comedy was titled Nature's Way, so the plural noun is the possessive word in that title.

clue.text: Sea nymph gets smaller gin cocktail from titled novelist

parts.note: Doris was a sea nymph of Greek myth, wife of Nereus
smaller means less in quantity

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of gin are mixed up

explanation.surface: A mermaid shrinks a mixed drink for a distinguished author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' mixes GIN into ING. 'titled' points to the honour she held, Companion of Honour, and the name is the title of the person.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris Lessing was a Nobel-winning British author of fiction, honoured as a Companion of Honour.

clue.text: Mrs Gaskell offers credit on a new car

parts.note: CR is the bookkeeping abbreviation for credit
a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: A dealer offers finance on a brand-new car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mrs Gaskell offers' is the definition: the Victorian novelist Elizabeth Gaskell offers a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranford is Elizabeth Gaskell's novel of genteel village life, so it is what she offers readers.

clue.text: Found inept, but full of spirit

indicators.note: the words Found inept are full of, that is contain, the answer spanning them

explanation.surface: Someone judged incompetent who is nonetheless lively and brimming with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of spirit' looks like praise for a lively person; 'spirit' is the definition, a supernatural being.
explanation.definitionFit: An undine is a water sprite of folklore, a female elemental being.

clue.text: He introduced old friends

parts.note: Clive ... published Old Friends (1956), memoirs that present his Bloomsbury companions to readers

explanation.surface: A host making introductions between friends of long standing.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a social host; it is the critic Clive Bell, whose memoir Old Friends presented his Bloomsbury circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Clive Bell, art critic of the Bloomsbury Group, wrote the memoir Old Friends about his companions.

clue.text: Cathedral town's Fleming is delightful

parts.note: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire; the possessive gives the S
Ian Fleming, creator of James Bond

explanation.surface: A man from a cathedral city named Fleming is charming.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysian means heavenly or blissful, from Elysium, the paradise of Greek myth.

clue.text: Property tied up? 3 booked it

parts.note: land is real property
locked means secured or tied up

explanation.surface: Real estate whose title is tied up, and a reservation made for it.
explanation.walkthrough: '3 booked it' means the writer at 3-down put it in a book: it is a volume of her Children of Violence sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Landlocked (1965) is the fourth novel of Doris Lessing's Children of Violence series.

clue.text: Perhaps rid art, and love, of holding back

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given could be arranged another way

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Freeing art and love from restraint, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' anagrams RIDARTAND plus O (love).
explanation.definitionFit: Ritardando is the musical direction to slow down gradually, a holding back of tempo.

clue.text: Farrell's alter ego in Harry Andrews

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters across the two words of the name

explanation.surface: An actor named Harry Andrews playing the novelist Farrell's double.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Andrews was a British actor, so the name looks like casting news.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddie Ryan is the autobiographical hero of James T. Farrell's later novels, the author's fictional self.

clue.text: Many a sea film adapted from 14's work

indicators.note: adapting a work changes it into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A movie about the ocean adapted from a novelist's book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges MANYASEAFILM.
explanation.definitionFit: My Life as a Man (1974) is a novel by the writer at 14-down, Philip Roth.

clue.text: Indian costume exceptionally worn by Egyptian lady-in-waiting

indicators.note: worn in an exceptional way, so the garment's letters are put on in a new order

parts.note: a sari is the draped garment of Indian women

explanation.surface: A sari worn in an unusual way by an attendant at the Egyptian court.
explanation.definitionFit: Iras is one of Cleopatra's attendant women in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: Saucy recollections from admirer, on New York eminence

parts.note: a fan is an admirer
an eminence is a raised piece of ground

explanation.surface: Racy memories of a fan atop a high point in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cleland's erotic novel takes the form of a woman's memoirs, so its heroine's name stands for racy reminiscences.

clue.text: Boost anger, say, in American writer

indicators.note: say signals that the two words are spoken and the sound gives the name

parts.note: a fillip is a stimulus or boost; wrath is anger

explanation.surface: A writer from the USA who gets a lift from rage.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, FILLIP WRATH sounds like the novelist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Roth was the American novelist of Portnoy's Complaint and American Pastoral.

clue.text: "Codlin diminished the distance between himself and the —" (The Old Curiosity Shop)

definitions.text: "Codlin diminished the distance between himself and the —" (The Old Curiosity Shop)

parts.words: "Codlin diminished the distance between himself and the —" (The Old Curiosity Shop)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Dickens: the Punch-man Codlin walks faster toward an inn

explanation.surface: A line from Dickens's novel with its last word left out.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostelry is an inn, the place the thirsty showman Codlin hurries towards in Dickens's novel.

clue.text: Déjeuner sur l'Herbe offered by Inge

explanation.surface: A famous Manet painting presented by the American playwright William Inge.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunch on the grass is an outdoor meal, and Picnic (1953) is William Inge's Pulitzer-winning play.

clue.text: One recognizing heroism may be key rival

indicators.note: may be signals that the letters could form something else

explanation.surface: Someone who honours bravery might turn out to be a chief competitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges KEYRIVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth the Valkyries choose the bravest of the slain warriors and carry them to Valhalla.

clue.text: King's English from Meynell

parts.note: Louis is the name of many French kings

explanation.surface: The monarch's tongue as used by the writer Meynell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King's English' reads as correct speech; it is a French king's name plus E. The definition is a title from the Meynell family of writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Louise is the title of a work by Viola Meynell, of the literary Meynell family.

clue.text: Some of Browne's income, so to speak?

definitions.text: Some of Browne's income, so to speak?

parts.words: Some of Browne's income, so to speak?
parts.note: Sir Thomas Browne wrote Urn Burial, so his takings are urn-based, a word said like earnings

explanation.surface: A question about part of someone named Browne's pay.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Thomas Browne's Hydriotaphia, or Urn Burial, is about burial urns; the urn-related word sounds like earnings, that is income.
explanation.definitionFit: Urnings means homosexual men, but here it stands as a play on income earned from urns.

clue.text: Work of Bemelmans and Emile perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given could be reordered

explanation.surface: A children's book by Ludwig Bemelmans, maybe featuring a boy called Emile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ANDEMILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeline is Ludwig Bemelmans's picture book about a little girl at a Paris boarding school.

clue.text: She danced with Duncan

parts.note: the woman is not a partner of someone called Duncan: Duncan is her own surname

explanation.surface: A woman who took the floor with a partner named Duncan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with Duncan' suggests a partner; it is the dancer's surname joined to her first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Isadora Duncan was the American pioneer of modern dance.

clue.text: Campion is a member of this group

definitions.text: Campion is a member of this group

parts.words: Campion is a member of this group
parts.note: the campion is a wild flower, and botanists place it in a genus of pinks

explanation.surface: A man named Campion belongs to some club.
explanation.walkthrough: Campion looks like the poet Thomas Campion or detective Albert Campion; it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Silene is the plant genus of campions and catchflies in the pink family.

clue.text: Producers of a successful writing collaboration

definitions.text: Producers of a successful writing collaboration

parts.words: Producers of a successful writing collaboration
parts.note: not two co-authors but the two tools that together make handwriting

explanation.surface: The authors of a hit co-written book.
explanation.walkthrough: The writing collaboration looks like two authors; it is the nib and its fluid working together.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing by hand needs both an instrument and the fluid it lays down, a partnership that produces script.

clue.text: Strange closure where Thurber retired?

parts.note: a closure is a fastening, and a famous James Thurber cartoon puts a barking sea animal on a bedhead

explanation.surface: An odd shutdown at the humorist Thurber's retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: Thurber's cartoon has a wife in bed saying 'All right, have it your way, you heard a seal bark!' with the animal on the headboard: the closure, a fastening, is also that beast in the bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal fastens an envelope or jar, and the animal sits over the bed where Thurber's couple retire.

clue.text: Offered by Cronin as openers for the domain

definitions.text: Offered by Cronin as openers for the domain

parts.words: Offered by Cronin as openers for the domain
parts.note: A. J. Cronin's novel names the things that open the Kingdom, a domain

explanation.surface: Something a man named Cronin handed over to unlock an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A. J. Cronin wrote The Keys of the Kingdom; locks open with these, and a kingdom is a domain.

clue.text: Has start of old war novel, supposedly

indicators.note: the start of each of the next four words, taken in order

explanation.surface: Someone has the beginning of an old war novel, or so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' applies to each of 'old war novel, supposedly', not just 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to have it.

clue.text: Artist in one-rhyme, or free format

indicators.note: free format means no fixed form, so the letters are set out freely in a new order

explanation.surface: A poet working in a single-rhyme scheme or in free verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free format' rearranges ONERHYMEOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Moore was the English sculptor of large reclining figures.

clue.text: Wells's headmaster with the patience of Job

definitions.text: Wells's headmaster with the patience of Job

parts.words: Wells's headmaster with the patience of Job
parts.note: H. G. Wells's The Undying Fire retells the Book of Job through a long-suffering headmaster named Job

explanation.surface: A head teacher in the town of Wells who is endlessly patient.
explanation.walkthrough: Wells looks like the cathedral city, which has famous schools; it is H. G. Wells, whose headmaster is literally named Job.
explanation.definitionFit: Job Huss is the suffering schoolmaster of H. G. Wells's The Undying Fire.

clue.text: Hardy works that keep on coming up

definitions.text: Hardy works that keep on coming up

parts.words: Hardy works that keep on coming up
parts.note: not novels by Thomas Hardy but tough plants that return every year

explanation.surface: Thomas Hardy's novels that keep cropping up.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy looks like Thomas Hardy the novelist; it is the gardener's sense, plants able to survive winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that come up year after year are long-lived growers, and the hardy kind survive frost.
